question: Who among the following led the Dandi March in March 1930?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Mahatma Gandhi**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• **Mahatma Gandhi** led the **Dandi March**, also known as the **Salt March**, on **12 March 1930**, starting from the Sabarmati Ashram in Ahmedabad.
 
• The march was a 24-day nonviolent protest against the British salt monopoly, covering a distance of approximately **240 miles** (384 kilometers) to the coastal village of Dandi in Gujarat.
 
• The primary objective was to protest the British-imposed **Salt Tax**, which deprived Indians of the ability to produce or sell salt independently.
 
• On **6 April 1930**, Gandhi reached Dandi and symbolically broke the salt laws by producing salt from seawater, marking the beginning of the **Civil Disobedience Movement**.
 
• The march included thousands of supporters and inspired a nationwide movement against British rule, emphasizing Gandhi's philosophy of **nonviolent resistance (Satyagraha)**.
